cases.name: container berth turnaround control
cases.prompt: A port operations director needs a product for the morning vessel call at Pier 7. The berth planner, terminal superintendent, harbor pilot, and crane dispatcher must reconcile container discharge, quay crane availability, tug window, and berth occupancy before the vessel can sail. Keep carrier manifests as evidence, record weather holds separately, and do not infer customs clearance from terminal events.

cases.name: channel dredging permit ledger
cases.prompt: The harbor authority wants a workspace to coordinate channel dredging before the spring shipping season. A dredging contractor submits bathymetric survey files, the environmental monitor records turbidity samples, and the port engineer compares the approved dredge prism with removal quantities. The system must distinguish a permit condition from a completed disposal load and preserve the USACE review boundary.

cases.name: reefer customs release chain
cases.prompt: A cold-chain logistics provider needs a release workflow for imported reefer containers carrying fresh berries. The import broker uploads the phytosanitary certificate, the customs broker confirms the entry status, and the cold-store manager checks the pulp temperature before assigning a delivery slot. The product must retain the inspection hold reason and never treat an appointment as proof of customs release.

cases.name: inland port intermodal appointment
cases.prompt: An inland port operator wants to reduce missed handoffs between drayage trucks and the intermodal rail ramp. Dispatchers need to match a chassis number, gate appointment, rail cut-off, and interchange receipt for each export load. Railroad staff own train acceptance, while the port owns gate operations; a driver check-in cannot establish that a container made the scheduled train.

cases.name: airport deicing material readiness
cases.prompt: A snow operations manager at a regional airport needs to decide whether the deicing program is ready before an overnight storm. Ramp supervisors report glycol inventory, mechanics report truck calibration, and the airport operations center receives runway friction readings. The product should show FAA inspection evidence, distinguish a forecast from a closure decision, and retain the Type IV fluid concentration used on each truck.

cases.name: regional air cargo acceptance
cases.prompt: A regional cargo airline needs a first-use flow for accepting a time-critical medical shipment. The freight forwarder presents an air waybill, the warehouse agent verifies dangerous goods declaration status, and the loadmaster assigns a ULD position after weighing the shipment. Do not claim flight departure from warehouse acceptance; retain the shipper temperature range and the airline acceptance timestamp as separate evidence.

cases.name: airfield wildlife strike evidence
cases.prompt: An airport wildlife biologist needs a case-management product after a bird strike near Runway 18. The air traffic controller supplies the occurrence time, the maintenance crew logs aircraft damage, and the biologist records species identification with a DNA sample reference. Preserve the FAA wildlife hazard assessment boundary, and do not convert a pilot report into a confirmed species record without laboratory evidence.

cases.name: airline rotable parts quarantine
cases.prompt: An airline maintenance control center needs to manage a suspect rotable part removed from an A320 during a line check. The technician creates the removal record, quality assurance evaluates the service bulletin, and stores quarantine the actuator pending engineering disposition. The system must keep the serialized actuator, airworthiness release, and non-routine card linked while preventing a stock transfer from being treated as a return-to-service approval.

cases.name: freight rail geometry exception
cases.prompt: A Class I railroad track supervisor needs a focused workflow for a geometry car exception on a heavy-haul subdivision. The inspection analyst uploads the track geometry run, the signal maintainer notes a crossing condition, and the dispatcher applies a slow order only after engineering review. Keep FRA defect criteria, milepost location, and tamping completion as separate facts; a work order closeout is not proof that the speed restriction was lifted.

cases.name: rail crew qualification handoff
cases.prompt: A short-line railroad needs to assign a relief crew after a delayed grain train reaches a remote terminal. The crew caller checks hours of service, the locomotive engineer confirms route qualification, and the conductor records the brake test before departure. The product must respect union roster evidence, distinguish a crew call from a crew acceptance, and retain the train symbol, terminal bulletin, and positive train control status.

cases.name: commuter rail traction outage
cases.prompt: A commuter rail agency needs a coordinated response when a traction power substation trips during the evening peak. The power controller reports the SCADA alarm, the field electrician verifies breaker position, and the rail operations manager authorizes a bus bridge. Preserve the relay event log, feeder isolation, and passenger advisory as distinct records, because a restored voltage reading does not alone certify safe train movement.

cases.name: hazmat trucking route release
cases.prompt: A bulk chemical carrier needs a dispatch product for a sodium hypochlorite delivery crossing two state lines. The planner selects an approved hazmat route, the driver completes a pre-trip inspection, and the safety officer reviews the emergency response guide. Retain the bill of lading, placard class, tank wash certificate, and route restriction; do not treat GPS arrival as evidence that the consignee accepted the load.

cases.name: electric delivery fleet charge dispatch
cases.prompt: A city delivery fleet manager needs to plan morning routes for electric vans after several chargers reported faults. The dispatcher sees state of charge, the facilities electrician confirms charger availability, and drivers report refrigerated cargo needs. The system must preserve kWh readings, route reserve threshold, charger fault code, and vehicle assignment while keeping charger repair ownership separate from fleet dispatch approval.

cases.name: tanker fleet vapor recovery audit
cases.prompt: A fuel distributor needs an audit-ready workflow for gasoline tanker loading at a terminal rack. The terminal operator records vapor recovery pressure, the driver signs the loading ticket, and the environmental compliance lead reviews the vapor tightness test. Keep compartment seal numbers, API gravity, loading rack authorization, and test date visible; a signed ticket cannot replace the compliance lead's determination.

cases.name: offshore wind service transfer
cases.prompt: An offshore wind operator needs a service-transfer decision for technicians scheduled to inspect a turbine gearbox. The marine coordinator reviews wave height, the vessel master confirms transfer limits, and the wind technician records lockout-tagout status before climbing. Preserve the turbine identifier, sea-state forecast, gearbox oil sample, and permit-to-work; a vessel departure is not evidence that personnel transferred safely.

cases.name: transmission vegetation clearance
cases.prompt: A transmission utility needs to schedule vegetation work below a 230 kV line before wildfire season. The arborist documents conductor clearance, the grid operator sets an outage window, and the landowner liaison confirms access consent. The product must retain LiDAR survey evidence, minimum approach distance, easement boundary, and work completion photos without claiming that a trimming request granted electrical clearance.

cases.name: solar inverter curtailment review
cases.prompt: A utility-scale solar operator needs an incident workflow after inverter strings underperform at noon. The control room records SCADA telemetry, the field technician captures IV curve measurements, and the market operator issues a curtailment instruction. Keep DC combiner status, irradiance sensor reading, curtailment interval, and inverter serial number distinct, because reduced output can result from either a grid limit or equipment fault.

cases.name: gas pipeline integrity dig
cases.prompt: A pipeline integrity manager needs a controlled plan for an anomaly excavation on a high-pressure transmission line. The inline inspection analyst provides the metal-loss feature, the excavation contractor confirms safe digging, and the corrosion engineer assesses remaining strength. Preserve the MFL signal, coating holiday, MAOP, and hydrostatic test history; do not let a completed excavation stand in for engineering acceptance of the repair.

cases.name: concrete pour quality release
cases.prompt: A bridge contractor needs a first-path workflow for approving a nighttime concrete pour on a pier cap. The batch plant sends the mix ticket, the field inspector records slump and air content, and the structural engineer reviews cylinder break results. Keep the pour sequence, curing blanket, compressive strength, and engineer release traceable; a truck arrival must not be treated as acceptance of the concrete placement.

cases.name: bridge bearing replacement closure
cases.prompt: A state transportation agency needs to coordinate a weekend bridge bearing replacement over an active freight corridor. The bridge engineer approves the jack plan, the rail dispatcher grants a track window, and the contractor measures bearing elevation before reopening lanes. Preserve the detour notice, load rating, track protection, and survey reading as separate evidence, because lane reopening does not prove the rail window was properly released.

cases.name: tunnel ventilation smoke test
cases.prompt: A tunnel operator needs to conduct a ventilation smoke test before commissioning a new emergency fan. The fire marshal observes the drill, the mechanical contractor logs fan RPM, and the control center records airflow direction. Keep the smoke test duration, CO sensor level, damper position, and emergency response observation grounded in the record; a fan start command is not proof that smoke control met the design scenario.

cases.name: water utility main break isolation
cases.prompt: A municipal water utility needs an incident product for a trunk main break affecting a hospital district. The dispatcher receives pressure alarms, the field crew closes isolation valves, and the water quality lead collects chlorine residual samples before a boil-water advisory is lifted. Preserve the valve turn record, pressure zone, bacteriological sample, and public notice approval; service restoration alone cannot prove water quality clearance.

cases.name: wastewater nutrient permit response
cases.prompt: A wastewater treatment plant needs to manage a nutrient excursion during a wet-weather event. The operator records influent flow, the laboratory reports total phosphorus, and the compliance manager reviews the NPDES permit limit before submitting a notice. Keep the composite sample, aeration basin condition, permit exceedance, and corrective action distinct; a rainfall forecast is context, not evidence of a discharge violation.

cases.name: hospital chiller redundancy drill
cases.prompt: A hospital facilities director needs to run a chiller redundancy drill without disrupting surgical suites. The building engineer reports chilled-water supply temperature, the infection prevention lead defines occupied-area constraints, and the vendor technician tests the backup chiller. Preserve the BMS trend, differential pressure, generator contingency, and clinical sign-off; a successful equipment start is not approval to expose patient areas to a temperature excursion.

cases.name: university laboratory exhaust certification
cases.prompt: A university facilities team needs to certify laboratory exhaust after renovating a chemistry teaching lab. The commissioning agent measures face velocity, the environmental health officer checks fume hood performance, and the department chair accepts the room schedule. Keep the tracer gas result, sash position, airflow balance, and certification date grounded in the record; a room reservation must not imply that the hood passed certification.

cases.name: data center generator fuel transfer
cases.prompt: A data center operations lead needs to coordinate a planned generator fuel transfer before hurricane season. The critical facilities engineer verifies generator load, the fuel vendor provides the delivery certificate, and the security manager grants dock access. Preserve the ATS test, fuel-water sample, tank level, and change window, while ensuring a vendor arrival does not substitute for the operations lead's completed transfer approval.

cases.name: semiconductor fab tool qualification
cases.prompt: A semiconductor fab needs to qualify a replacement etch chamber after maintenance. The process engineer reviews wafer map results, the equipment technician records chamber seasoning, and quality assurance checks particle counts before production release. Retain the RF power setting, endpoint recipe, particle monitor, and lot disposition; a completed maintenance ticket cannot demonstrate that the process window is stable.

cases.name: chemical plant batch deviation
cases.prompt: A specialty chemical plant needs to review a batch deviation after reactor temperature exceeded the operating range. The board operator supplies the batch record, the process chemist analyzes the GC result, and the quality manager decides whether to release the material. Keep the reaction temperature, agitator speed, GC chromatogram, and deviation number distinct, because a finished batch does not itself prove product conformance.

cases.name: food plant allergen changeover
cases.prompt: A ready-meal manufacturer needs a verifiable allergen changeover between a sesame recipe and a sesame-free production run. The sanitation lead records ATP swabs, the line supervisor confirms label reconciliation, and quality assurance reviews the allergen test strip. Preserve the CIP cycle, production code, allergen matrix, and release decision; a cleaned line status must not replace the quality review.

cases.name: textile mill dye bath release
cases.prompt: A textile mill needs to approve a dye bath before running a customer color standard. The colorist measures spectrophotometer values, the production manager confirms fabric lot availability, and the wastewater operator reviews discharge capacity. Keep the dye recipe, pH reading, Delta E value, and lot card evidence connected, because a color match sample cannot alone authorize the full production run.

cases.name: vineyard frost irrigation allocation
cases.prompt: A vineyard operations manager needs to allocate frost-protection irrigation across blocks before dawn. The viticulturist reports bud stage, the irrigation technician confirms pump capacity, and the water district liaison provides allocation limits. Preserve the wet-bulb temperature, block moisture probe, water right, and pump runtime; a weather alert is not proof that irrigation may exceed the allocation.

cases.name: grain elevator fumigation clearance
cases.prompt: A grain elevator manager needs to release a bin after phosphine fumigation before loading export wheat. The licensed applicator logs gas concentration, the safety coordinator verifies confined-space entry controls, and the merchandiser schedules the railcar. Keep the fumigant exposure period, grain lot, clearance reading, and applicator license visible; a railcar reservation cannot establish that the bin is safe for entry.

cases.name: dairy herd cooling outage
cases.prompt: A dairy cooperative needs a response plan after a bulk tank cooling alarm at a member farm. The farmer reports milk temperature, the field technician evaluates compressor current, and the quality manager decides whether to hold the pickup. Preserve the somatic cell count, bulk tank volume, temperature trend, and pickup hold decision, because a repaired compressor does not prove the milk remains within quality limits.

cases.name: produce packing traceability hold
cases.prompt: A produce packing house needs to place a traceability hold after a retailer reports a possible foreign-material finding. The food safety manager links the harvest crew record, the packing supervisor identifies the line run, and the logistics coordinator stops pallet dispatch. Keep the field block, wash-water sanitizer level, carton code, and hold notice grounded; a shipment scan must not be treated as proof that every affected pallet was located.

cases.name: pharmaceutical cold-chain excursion
cases.prompt: A pharmaceutical distributor needs to investigate a refrigerated shipment that exceeded its validated lane temperature during an airport delay. The quality unit reviews the data logger, the carrier provides the chain-of-custody record, and the manufacturer assesses stability data. Preserve the excursion duration, Mean Kinetic Temperature, shipment seal, and disposition decision; a delivery signature cannot establish product suitability for release.

cases.name: critical spare parts allocation
cases.prompt: A mining company needs to allocate one critical haul-truck hydraulic pump between two sites after both report failures. The maintenance planner verifies the part number, the reliability engineer compares failure analysis, and the site superintendent approves the transport priority. Keep the serialized pump, equipment downtime, warranty status, and transfer authorization distinct; an inventory count cannot prove that either repair is technically ready.

cases.name: urban pavement emergency repair
cases.prompt: A city public works department needs to prioritize an emergency pavement repair after a bus route reports a deep pothole. The inspector documents the distress rating, the traffic engineer approves the lane closure, and the contractor records asphalt temperature during placement. Preserve the work zone permit, compaction test, pavement section, and reopening inspection; a citizen complaint does not establish that the repair meets specification.

cases.name: floodgate actuator maintenance
cases.prompt: A flood control district needs to schedule actuator maintenance before forecast river levels rise. The hydraulic technician records cylinder pressure, the operations chief confirms gate position, and the environmental coordinator checks fish-passage restrictions. Keep the SCADA command history, seal inspection, river stage, and maintenance release traceable; a forecast crest cannot authorize work inside the restricted operating window.

cases.name: telecom tower generator inspection
cases.prompt: A telecom infrastructure operator needs to inspect a remote tower generator after a wildfire-related utility outage. The field technician captures battery voltage, the network operations center checks backhaul availability, and the land manager grants road access. Preserve the generator runtime, RF alarm, fuel level, and access authorization, because a restored carrier signal does not prove the site has enough fuel for the next outage period.

cases.name: aggregate quarry haul road control
cases.prompt: A quarry manager needs to reopen a haul road after heavy rain created a slope failure near the crusher. The geotechnical engineer reviews inclinometer readings, the fleet supervisor checks truck braking condition, and the safety manager approves the traffic plan. Keep the berm height, slope inspection, haul route, and blasting exclusion boundary explicit; a grader pass is not evidence that loaded trucks may return safely.
